source_text: 1. Proprer hoc autem ad passionem veniens, ut evangelisaret Abrahee, et iis qui cum eo, apertionem heereditatis, cum gratias egisset tenens calicem, et bibisset ab eo, et dedisset discipulis, dicebat eis: Bibite ex co omnes. Hic est sanguis meus novi Testamenti, qui pro multis effundetur in remissionem peccatorum, Dico autem vobis, a modo non bibam de generatione vitis hujus, usque diem illum, quando illum bibam vobiscum novum in regno Patris mei. Utique hereditatem terree ipse novabit, et reintegrabit mysterium gloriz filiorum; quemadmodum David ait: Qui IrePromisit bibere de generatione vitis cum suis discipulis, utrumque ostendens, et hzereditatem terre in qua bibitur nova generatio vitis, et carnalem resurrectionem disciQuze enim nova resurgit caro, ipsa est que et Neque autem sursum in superceelesti novyum percepit poculum, loco constitutus cum suis, potest intelligi bibens vitis generationem ; neque rursus sine carne sunt, qui bibunt illud: ecarnis enim proprium est et non spiritus, qui ex vite accipitur potus. 2, Et propter hoc dicebat Dominus: 2Cum facis prandium, vel coenam, noli vocare divites, neque amicos et vicinos et cognatos, ne ipsi invicem vocent te, et fiat retributio ab eis: sed voca claudos caecos, mendicos, et beatus eris, quoniam non habent retribuere tibi: retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum. Et iterum ait: Quicunque dimiserit agros, aut domos, aut parentes, aut fratres, aut. Jilios propter me, centuplum accipiet in hoc seculo, et in futuro enim sunt in hoc seeculo centupla, et prandia exhibita pauperibus, et coenze que redduntur? Heec sunt in Regni temporibus, hoc est in septima die, que est sanctificata, in qua requievit Deus ab omnibus operibus quze fecit, — que est yerum justorum sabbatum, in qua non facient omne Deo, pascentem eos epulis omnibus. 3. Quemadmodum et Isaac continet benedictio, qua benefilium minorem Jacob: Ecce, dicens, odor filii mei, quasi odor agri pleni, quem benedixit Deus. Ager autem mundus est, et propterea addidit: Det tibi Deus de rore cali, et a fertilitate adorent te principes, et esto dominus \fratris tui, et adorabunt te Qui maledicet te, maledictus erit; et qui benefilii patris tut. dicet te, benedictus erit. Heee ergo si non quis accipiat ad preefinita Regni, in grandem contradictionem et contrarietatem incidet, Squemadmodum Judzi incidentes in omni aporia constituuntur. Non solum enim in hae vita huic Jacob non servierunt gentes ; sed et post benedictionem ipse profectus, servivit avunculo suo Laban Syro annos viginti: et non tantum non est factus dominus fratris sui, sed et ipse Esau adoravit fratrem suum, quando reversus est a Mesopotamia ad patrem, et munera multa obtulit ei. Multitudinem autem tritici et vini quomodo hereditavit hic, qui propter famem factam in terra, in qua habitabat, in A¢gyptum transmigravit, subjectus Pharaoni, qui tune regnabat in A¢gypto ? Preedicta itaque benedictio ad tempora Regni sine contradictione quando regnabunt justi surgentes a mortuis: quando et creatura renovata, et liberata, multitudinem fructificabit universze escee, ex rore cceli, et ex fertilitate terrae: quemadmodum 3 Presbyteri meminerunt, qui Johannem discipulum Domini viderunt, audisse se ab eo, quemadmodum de temporibus illis docebat et dicebat: 4‘¢ Venient dies, in quibus vineze nascentur, singule decem millia palmitum habentes, et in uno palmite dena millia brachiorum, et in uno vero palmite dena millia flagellorum, et in unoquoque flagello dena millia botruum, et in unoquoque otro dena millia acinorum, et unumquodque acinum expressum. dabit vigintiquinque metretas vini. Et cum eorum apprehenderit aliquis sanctorum botrum, alius clamabit; Botrus ego melior sum, me sume, per me Dominum benedic.’ Similiter et granum tritici decem millia spicarum generaturum, et unamquamque spicam habituram decem millia granorum, et unumquodque granum quinque bilibres similze claree mundz: et reliqua autem poma, et semina, et herbam secundum congruentiam iis consequentem: et omnia animalia iis cibis utentia que a terra accipiuntur, pacifica et consentanea invicem fieri, subjecta hominibus cum omni subjectione*.” 4. Hee autem et Papias Johannis auditor, Polycarpi autem contubernalis, vetus homo, per scripturam testimonium perhibet, in quarto librorum suorum: sunt enim illi quinque libri conseripti. Et adjecit, dicens : “‘ Heee autem credibilia sunt credentibus. Et Juda,” inquit, proditore non credente, et interrogante : Quomodo ergo tales genituree a Domino perficientur?” dixisse Dominum : * Videbunt qui venient in illa.”| Heee ergo tempora prophetans Hsaias ait: Lt compascetur lupus cum agno, et pardus conquiescet cum heedo, et vitulus et taurus et leo simul pascentur, et puer pusillus ducet eos. Et bos et ursus simul pascentur, et simul infantes eorum erunt: et leo et bos manducabunt paleas. Et puer infans cavernam aspidum, et in cubile filiorum aspidum manumi mittet, et non male facient, nec poterunt perdere aliquem in monte sancto meo. Et iterum recapitulans ait: Tune Jupi et agni simul, et leo quasi bos vescetur paleis, serpens autem terram quasi panem: et non nocebunt, neque vexabunt in monte sancto dicit Dominus. Non ignoro autem, quoniam quidam hee in feros et ex diversis gentibus, et variis operibus credentes, et cum crediderint consentientes justis, tentent transferre. etsi nunc hoc sit in quibusdam hominibus, ex variis gentibus in unam sententiam fidei venientibus, nihilominus in rejustorum super iis animalibus, quemadmodum dictum est: Dives enim in omnibus Deus. Et oportet conditione revocata, obedire et subjecta esse omnia animalia homini, et ad primam a Deo datam reverti escam, ‘(quemadmodum autem in obedientia subjecta erant Adze,) fructum terree. Alias autem et est nunc ostendere leonem paleis vesci. Hoc autem signifieabat magnitudinem et pinguedinem fructuum. Si enim leo animal paleis vescitur; quale ipsum triticum erit, cujus palea ad escam congrua erit leonum ?
pass_a_gloss: For this reason, coming to the passion, in order that he might evangelize Abraham and those who are with him, the opening of the inheritance, when he had given thanks, holding the cup, and had drunk from it, and had given it to the disciples, he was saying to them: Drink from it, all of you. This is my blood of the new Testament, which will be poured out for many for the remission of sins. I say to you, from now on I will not drink of the generation of this vine, until that day when I will drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father. Indeed, he himself will renew the inheritance of the earth and will restore the mystery of the glorification of the sons; just as David says: Who promised to drink of the generation of the vine with his disciples, showing both the inheritance of the earth in which the new generation of the vine is drunk, and the carnal resurrection of the disciples. For the new flesh which rises again, it is the same which also, and not the spirit, which is taken from the drink of the vine. For it is proper to the flesh, and not to the spirit, which is taken from the vine. And for this reason the Lord was saying: When you make a dinner or a supper, do not invite the rich, nor friends and neighbors and relatives, lest they also invite you in return, and it becomes a repayment from them: but invite the lame, the blind, the poor, and you will be blessed, because they do not have anything to repay you: for it will be repaid to you in the resurrection of the just. And again he says: Whoever leaves fields, or houses, or parents, or brothers, or children for my sake, will receive a hundredfold in this age, and in the future, for in this age there are a hundredfold, and dinners are offered to the poor, and suppers which are returned. These are in the times of the Kingdom, that is, in the seventh day, which is sanctified, in which God rested from all the works which he made, — which is truly the Sabbath of the just, in which they will not do all things to God, feeding them with all delights. Just as also Isaac contains a blessing, by which he blesses the younger Jacob: Behold, he says, the smell of my son, like the smell of a full field, which God has blessed. And the field is the world, and therefore he added: May God give you of the dew of heaven, and of the fertility of the earth, may the princes adore you, and may you be the lord of your brother, and may they adore you. Whoever curses you will be cursed; and whoever blesses you will be blessed. These things, therefore, if someone does not receive them according to the predestined times of the Kingdom, will fall into great contradiction and contrariety, just as the Jews, falling into every difficulty, are established. For not only in this life did the nations not serve this Jacob; but also after the blessing, he himself, having set out, served his uncle Laban, a Syrian, for twenty years: and not only was he not made the lord of his brother, but also Esau adored his brother, when he returned from Mesopotamia to his father, and offered many gifts to him. But how did he inherit a multitude of wheat and wine, who, because of the famine made in the land in which he lived, migrated to Egypt, subject to Pharaoh, who then reigned in Egypt? The aforementioned blessing, therefore, pertains to the times of the Kingdom without contradiction, when the just, rising from the dead, will reign: when also the creation, renewed and liberated, will produce a multitude of fruits, from the dew of heaven and from the fertility of the earth: just as the presbyters remembered, who saw John, the disciple of the Lord, and heard from him, as he was teaching and saying: 'There will come days, in which vines will be born, each having ten thousand branches, and on one branch ten thousand shoots, and on one shoot ten thousand clusters, and on each cluster ten thousand grapes, and each grape, when pressed, will give twenty-five measures of wine. And when one of the saints takes hold of a cluster, another will cry out: I am a better cluster, take me, and through me bless the Lord.' Similarly, also a grain of wheat will produce ten thousand ears, and each ear will have ten thousand grains, and each grain will have five pounds of the purest wheat: and the rest of the fruits, and seeds, and herbs, according to their congruity, will follow: and all the animals, using these foods which are taken from the earth, will become peaceful and harmonious with each other, subject to humans with all subjection. But Papias, the hearer of John, and the companion of Polycarp, an old man, bears witness through scripture, in the fourth book of his writings: for there are five books written by him. And he adds, saying: 'These things are believable to those who believe. And Judas,' he says, 'the betrayer, not believing, and asking: How then will the Lord bring about such harvests?' the Lord said: 'Those who come into those times will see.' Therefore, prophesying about these times, Isaiah says: The wolf will feed with the lamb, and the leopard will rest with the kid, and the calf and the ox and the lion will feed together, and a little child will lead them. And the ox and the bear will feed together, and their young will be together: and the lion and the ox will eat straw. And a little child will put his hand into the den of the asp, and into the nest of the adder's young, and will not do harm, nor will they be able to destroy anyone in my holy mountain. And again, recapitulating, he says: Then the wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, and the serpent will eat the earth like bread: and they will not harm, nor will they vex, in my holy mountain, says the Lord. I am not unaware, however, that some, believing in the wild and from diverse nations, and various works, and having believed, consenting to the just, try to transfer these things. Although this may be the case in some men, from diverse nations, coming into one faith, nevertheless, in the resurrection of the just, over these animals, as has been said: For God is rich in all things. And it is necessary, the condition having been recalled, for all animals to obey and be subject to humans, and to return to the first food given by God, just as in obedience they were subject to Adam, the fruit of the earth. But now it is also shown that the lion eats straw. This, however, signifies the greatness and richness of the fruits. For if the lion, an animal, eats straw, what kind of wheat will it be, whose straw will be suitable as food for lions?

pass_b_english: For this reason he came to his passion: to preach the gospel to Abraham and those with him, opening the inheritance. Having given thanks, he took the cup, drank from it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, "Drink from it, all of you. This is my blood of the new Testament, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins" (Matt 26:27-28). I tell you, from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom (Matt 26:29). Indeed, he himself will renew the inheritance of the earth and restore the mystery of the glorification of the sons; just as David says: "Who promised to drink of the fruit of the vine with his disciples," showing both the inheritance of the earth in which the new fruit of the vine is drunk, and the bodily resurrection of the disciples (Ps 110:1; Acts 2:30-31). For the new flesh that rises is the very flesh that also receives the drink from the vine; it is proper to the flesh, not the spirit, to receive what comes from the vine. Neither can it be understood that he drinks the fruit of the vine up in a super-celestial place, seated there with his disciples; nor again are those who drink it without flesh, for it belongs to the flesh, not the spirit, to receive drink from the vine.

And for this reason the Lord said: "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite the rich, nor your friends, brothers, or relatives, lest they also invite you in return and you be repaid. But invite the lame, the blind, the poor, and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the just" (Luke 14:12-14). And again he says: "Whoever leaves fields, or houses, or parents, or brothers, or children for my sake will receive a hundredfold in this age, and in the age to come" (Matt 19:29; Mark 10:30). For in this age there are a hundredfold — meals given to the poor, and suppers that are returned. These belong to the times of the Kingdom, that is, the seventh day, which is sanctified, in which God rested from all the works he made (Gen 2:2-3) — which is truly the Sabbath of the just, in which they will not do every work for God, while he feeds them with every delight.

Just as Isaac contains the blessing by which he blessed the younger Jacob: "Behold, the smell of my son is like the smell of a full field, which God has blessed" (Gen 27:27). The field is the world, and therefore he added: "May God give you the dew of heaven, and the richness of the earth; may peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you" (Gen 27:28-29). If anyone does not receive these things according to the appointed times of the Kingdom, they will fall into great contradiction and contrariety, just as the Jews fall into every difficulty. For not only in this life did the nations not serve this Jacob; but after the blessing he went and served his uncle Laban the Syrian for twenty years (Gen 29-31). And not only was he not made lord over his brother, but Esau bowed down to his brother when he returned from Mesopotamia to his father, and offered him many gifts (Gen 33:3-11). How then did he inherit a multitude of wheat and wine, he who, because of the famine in the land where he lived, migrated to Egypt, subject to Pharaoh who then reigned in Egypt (Gen 46-47)? Therefore the aforementioned blessing pertains to the times of the Kingdom without contradiction, when the just, rising from the dead, will reign: when also the creation, renewed and set free, will produce an abundance of fruit from the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth (Rom 8:21). Just as the presbyters remembered, those who saw John the disciple of the Lord and heard from him how he taught about those times, saying: "Days will come when vines will grow, each having ten thousand branches, and on one branch ten thousand shoots, and on one shoot ten thousand clusters, and on each cluster ten thousand grapes, and each grape pressed will give twenty-five measures of wine. And when one of the saints takes hold of a cluster, another will cry out: 'I am a better cluster; take me, and through me bless the Lord.' Likewise a grain of wheat will produce ten thousand ears, and each ear will have ten thousand grains, and each grain will yield five pounds of the purest flour; and the rest of the fruits, seeds, and herbs will follow in like proportion. And all animals, feeding on these foods taken from the earth, will become peaceful and harmonious with one another, subject to humans in all subjection."

Papias, hearer of John and companion of Polycarp, an old man, bears witness in writing in the fourth of his five books. He adds: "These things are credible to those who believe. And Judas," he says, "the betrayer, not believing, asked: 'How then will the Lord accomplish such harvests?' The Lord said: 'Those who come into those times will see.'" Therefore Isaiah prophesies about these times: "The wolf will feed with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the kid; the calf and the young lion and the fatling together, and a little child will lead them" (Isaiah 11:6). "The cow and the bear will graze together; their young will lie down together; the lion will eat straw like the ox. The nursing child will play by the cobra's hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper's den. They will not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain" (Isaiah 11:7-8). And again, recapitulating, he says: "Then the wolf and the lamb will feed together, the lion will eat straw like the ox, and the serpent will eat dust like bread. They will not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain, says the Lord" (Isaiah 65:25). I am not unaware that some, believing these things to refer to wild beasts and diverse nations and various works, and having believed, consenting with the just, try to transfer them. Although this may happen now in some people, from diverse nations coming into one faith, nevertheless in the resurrection of the just, over these animals, as has been said — for God is rich in all things — it is necessary, the condition having been restored, that all animals obey and be subject to humans, and return to the first food given by God, just as they were subject to Adam in obedience, the fruit of the earth. But it is also shown now that the lion eats straw. This signifies the greatness and richness of the fruits. For if the lion, an animal, eats straw, what kind of wheat will it be, whose straw will be suitable food for lions?

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text, including the specific nuances of the millennium debate. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent English version with appropriate scripture citations (e.g., Matt 26:27-28, Isaiah 11:6) that match the content of the Latin. The translation of the Papias section and the Isaiah prophecy is consistent across both versions. The specific choices regarding 'centuplum' and 'adorabunt te' were correctly handled according to the provided lemmas.
